references.text: Both verses emphasize the inevitable destruction of the wicked and God's protection of the righteous as a theological constant.
Both verses illustrate the principle that the wicked fall by their own evil, while the righteous are preserved by God's righteousness.
The darkness, symbolizing both the downfall of the wicked and the trial of the faithful, creates a theological bridge between judgment and hope.
Both verses directly link the destruction of the wicked to the exaltation or security of the righteous.
Both verses use 'darkness/light' as an image of the downfall of the wicked and the watchfulness over the righteous.
The direct phrase 'not by their own strength' creates a unique theological connection between human weakness and God's sovereignty.
